title: Merge it and tidy up
concept: Merge the pull request, delete the branch, update local main

story.speaker: Priya
story.text: Approved. The hours were the last thing. Nice work.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Press the green Merge pull request button. That puts your branch into main.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Real sites also offer "Squash" and "Rebase" merges. Same changes, different history shape.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: We use the plain merge here. One button is enough to learn.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: After merging, delete the branch. It is finished, and old branches pile up fast.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Last step, and people forget it constantly: your local main is still old. Switch to it and pull.

items.text: Delete the finished branch on the website

hints: Three things: merge on the website, delete the branch there, then catch your own main up.
The Merge pull request button is on the pull request page. Afterwards use `git switch main` and `git pull`.
Press Merge pull request, then Delete branch. Then run `git switch main` and `git pull`.
recap: Merging a pull request puts the branch into main on the website. Your local main does not move until you pull. Delete finished branches to keep the list clean.

choices.text: Yes, merging updated my laptop too

predict.explanation: The merge happened on the website. Your laptop only learns about it when you fetch or pull.
